# How to become a yoga teacher | Thames Wellness Academy Journal

> How to become a yoga teacher in the UK: practise, complete an accredited course, then arrange insurance, first aid, and teaching experience. Free open days at Thames Wellness Academy.

Source: https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/how-to-become-a-yoga-teacher

To become a yoga teacher in the UK, build a consistent personal practice, complete an accredited teacher-training qualification, then obtain insurance, first-aid certification, and practical teaching experience. When you hesitate, come to an open day, or [call or message us](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/contact). You can always withdraw your registration.
        Before you apply
        200-hour entry requirements
        Who the Foundation course is for, and how to ask about experience, health, and payment plans.
        [What are the entry requirements for 200h teacher training](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/what-are-the-entry-requirements-for-200h-teacher-training)
        Free to attend
        Teacher training open days
- [Foundation Open Day, Saturday 21 November 2026, 12:00-2pm](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/open-day/)
- [CPD Open Day, Friday 29 January 2027](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/open-day/)
      The next Foundation Training Open Day is free: [Saturday 21 November 2026, 12:00-2pm](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/open-day/), in Berkshire and Reading. The CPD Open Day is also free: [Friday 29 January 2027](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/open-day/). The next [200-hour yoga teacher training](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/) begins on 12 February 2027 and runs across nine in-studio weekends to 14 November 2027.
      Thames Wellness Academy is a relevant local option if you are in or near Berkshire, Reading, or the wider Thames Valley. It offers teacher-led, on-site Foundation Training, CPD, and workshops, with Yoga Professionals Organisation Limited certification.
## Typical UK route
      Practise regularly. Most training providers expect a sustained personal practice before enrolment. Be familiar with common classes, breath work, and safe movement.
      Choose an accredited course. Common routes include a [200-hour Yoga Teacher Training](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/), a British Wheel of Yoga diploma, or a regulated Level 3/4 Diploma in Teaching Yoga.
        Next course
        200-hour yoga teacher training
        Begins 12 February 2027. Nine in-studio weekends in Berkshire and Reading, through to 14 November 2027.
        [View the 200-hour course](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/)
      Complete training and assessments. Courses typically cover asana, pranayama, anatomy and physiology, yoga philosophy, sequencing, class planning, safety, and supervised teaching practice.
      Meet professional requirements. Secure public-liability and professional-indemnity insurance plus a recognised first-aid and CPR certificate. Many studios and gyms expect these before you can teach.
        Before you teach
        Insurance and first aid
        Public-liability and professional-indemnity insurance, plus a recognised first-aid and CPR certificate.
      Build teaching experience. Start with community, online, cover, or studio classes, and consider registering with a professional body such as the Register of Exercise Professionals to demonstrate credibility to employers and clients.
## Where Thames Wellness Academy fits
      Thames Wellness Academy delivers yoga teacher training in Berkshire and Reading. Programmes are teacher-led and delivered on site across the Thames Valley. It offers Foundation Training, CPD, workshops, and retreats, and is certified by the Yoga Professionals Organisation Limited. Foundation pathways meet recognised standards for professional yoga and wellness teaching.
      For you, it sits in the "choose a recognised qualification" stage. The free Foundation Open Day on Saturday 21 November 2026 is the chance to meet faculty before you decide. The 200-hour course that follows begins on 12 February 2027.
            StageHow Thames Wellness Academy fits
              Decide your pathway
              Consider its Foundation Training if you want an in-person, locally delivered route in the Thames Valley. Come to the free Open Day on Saturday 21 November 2026, or the free CPD Open Day on Friday 29 January 2027.
              Gain a recognised qualification
              Its certification is through Yoga Professionals Organisation Limited. Verify the exact qualification level, contact hours, and accreditation details before enrolling. The next 200-hour course begins on 12 February 2027.
              Develop practical teaching skills
              Its on-site, teacher-led model may suit you if you value live feedback and supervised practice.
              Continue after qualifying
              Its CPD and workshops can support ongoing development after your initial training.
## Before enrolling
      Ask Thames Wellness Academy for:
- The exact qualification awarded, total contact hours, and whether it is equivalent to or includes a 200-hour teacher-training standard.
- Course dates, format, venue, cost, payment plans, and cancellation terms.
- Assessment requirements, including observed teaching practice and written or practical exams.
- Whether graduates receive support with insurance, first aid, mentoring, or finding teaching work.
- Confirmation of current accreditation and how it compares with Yoga Alliance Professionals, British Wheel of Yoga, or a regulated Level 3/4 qualification.
      There is no single statutory licence for teaching yoga in the UK. A credible accredited qualification, insurance, first-aid training, and supervised teaching experience are the practical foundations for working professionally.
        Still deciding
        Call or message us
        Ask about dates, cost, hours, and accreditation. You can withdraw your registration.

# What are the entry requirements for 200h teacher training | Thames Wellness Academy Journal

> Entry requirements for 200-hour yoga teacher training at Thames Wellness Academy. The pathway is for people new to teaching. Free Open Day, 21 November 2026.

Source: https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/what-are-the-entry-requirements-for-200h-teacher-training

Thames Wellness Academy does not publish a detailed formal entry-requirements list on the pages. Our main entry route is the [200-Hour Foundation Teacher Training](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/), and applicants are asked to [apply](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/join) or enquire so the Academy can assess their goals and experience. The 200-hour pathway is aimed at people who are new to teaching. Please take a moment to [send us an email](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/contact#email) or [give us a call](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/contact?course=callback#form). It will not oblige you to participate. We love to talk to you.
        Related reading
        How to become a yoga teacher
        The UK route from a personal practice to an accredited course, insurance, and teaching experience.
        [Read how to become a yoga teacher](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/how-to-become-a-yoga-teacher)
## 200-Hour Foundation Training
      Designed for newcomers to teaching. It runs over nine weekends from February to November 2027 and includes 180 contact hours plus 20 self-study hours. The next course begins on 12 February 2027 and finishes on 14 November 2027, in studio in Berkshire and Reading.
        Free to attend
        Foundation Open Day and 200-hour course
- [Foundation Open Day, Saturday 21 November 2026, 12:00-2pm](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/open-day/)
- [200-hour Foundation Training, from 12 February 2027](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/)
## 300-Hour Advanced Training
      Intended for people who are already qualified teachers and have completed a 200-hour certification. Foundation pathways continue through [Foundation Training](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/) toward 300 and 500 hours.
## CPD modules
      Intended for qualified yoga teachers, covering topics such as breathwork, [anatomy](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/functional-anatomy/), [pregnancy](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/pregnancy-yoga/), [sound](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/soundbath/), and [yoga nidra](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/yoga-nidra/). See the [CPD courses](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/). The free [CPD Open Day](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/open-day/) is Friday 29 January 2027.
## Studio workshops
      Open sessions on specialist themes. These provide a diploma of attendance. Yoga Professionals Organisation Limited certification applies to the teacher-training pathways. Browse [workshops](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/workshops/).
## Practical expectations
      Although not stated as formal prerequisites, you should expect to need:
- A genuine interest in yoga and a reasonable existing personal practice.
- Availability for the full in-person schedule, since core programmes are teacher-led and delivered on site in Berkshire and Reading.
- English sufficient to follow anatomy, teaching-method, and philosophy content.
- Commitment to complete both contact hours and self-study requirements.
- For the 300-hour or CPD routes, evidence of an existing 200-hour yoga teacher qualification.
      The [200-hour course page](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/) also asks for at least two years of regular yoga practice, or consistent class attendance with a recognised teacher, and readiness for weekend intensives.
## How to confirm eligibility
      The Academy directs prospective students to its [Apply page](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/join), where it asks about goals and experience, then helps match them to Foundation Training, CPD, or workshops. It also has a free Open Day for the 200-hour pathway on [21 November 2026, 12:00-2pm](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/open-day/), which would be the most direct way to ask about minimum experience, fitness or health considerations, application screening, and payment plans.
        No obligation
        Email or call
        Tell us your goals and experience. It will not oblige you to participate.

        [Register for the free Open Day](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/open-day/)
        [200-hour course](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/200-hour/)

# Breath work in professional teaching practice | Thames Wellness Academy Journal

> How diaphragmatic breath work supports stress regulation and safe, inclusive class delivery for wellness educators in Berkshire.

Source: https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/journal/breath-work-in-teaching

Breath work sits at the centre of professional teaching. Used well, it regulates stress responses, supports inclusive pacing and gives students a practical tool they can take beyond the mat.
## Why breath literacy matters
Teachers who understand diaphragmatic breathing can cue more safely in studio, corporate and therapeutic settings. The goal is not performance. It is steady nervous-system support and clear class craft.
## Practical teaching notes
- Introduce breath options rather than one rigid technique
- Watch for strain, dizziness or breath-holding under effort
- Link breath cues to movement only when students are ready
For structured training pathways, see [Foundation Training](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/foundation-yoga-training/) and specialist [workshops](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/workshops/).

# Evidence-informed wellness education | Thames Wellness Academy Journal

> Why research collaboration matters for credible teacher training and CPD programmes at Thames Wellness Academy.

Source: https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/journal/evidence-informed-wellness-education

Credible wellness education balances lived teaching experience with evidence from anatomy, physiology and applied research. That balance protects students and strengthens professional trust.
## What evidence-informed means here
It means curriculum that is updated with current understanding, faculty who can explain why a method is used, and assessment that values safe practice over trends.
## Where this shows up in courses
Foundation Training and CPD modules include anatomy depth and supervised teaching practice so graduates can apply learning with real people. Explore [courses](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/) or read about our [studio partners](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/research/partners/).

# Workshop highlights and practitioner tips | Thames Wellness Academy Journal

> Insights from specialist workshops on sleep health, menopause support and trauma-informed teaching.

Source: https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/journal/workshops-specialist-client-needs

Specialist workshops help teachers adapt for diverse client needs without abandoning foundations. Themes such as sleep health, menopause support and trauma-informed teaching require care, clarity and professional boundaries.
## Takeaways for class craft
- Offer choice and pacing options
- Use plain language for safety cues
- Know when to refer on rather than improvise
Browse upcoming specialist formats on the [workshops](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/workshops/) page, or continue with [CPD](https://thameswellnessacademy.co.uk/courses/cpd/).
